owned_process_regressions.scope: Actual newly spawned host subprocesses only; separate from real-service launch9.

publisher_regressions.prior_failure: Three impossible-count counterexamples failed on the old publisher; original private failure is preserved.

independent_review.method: Independent read-only helper/harness/test review plus independently executed narrow publisher correction regression and combined publication suite.
findings_closed: Original protected host-browser timeout gap is addressed by dedicated command session plus pre-exec command gate and separately registered browser process groups.

Private launcher acknowledgement precedes browser exec; kernel PID birth/group/UID identity is checked before owned signaling. Unknown, conflicted or incompletely observed ownership refuses successful proof.
Selector construction precedes child creation; initial identity/setup failure cannot execute the CLI and kills/reaps only the unreaped direct gated child.
Detached observed descendants and registered browser groups receive bounded TERM then KILL; unrelated groups and PID identity reuse are refused.
Normal/nonzero/timeout/exception are distinct; generic no-browser cleanup cannot qualify harness or publisher.
Publisher now enforces registeredBrowserGroups, termSignals and killSignals each <= trackedProcesses. All three impossible-count cases failed on old publisher and pass after correction.
limitations: No real Chrome, Docker, API, database or protected application gate executed by this reviewer.
Cleanup scope is registered POSIX groups and observed descendants, not arbitrary unobserved adversarial double-fork escapes.
PID/start observation plus signaling is not an atomic kernel capability against a hostile process-reuse race; untrusted/changed observed identities fail closed.
Kernel identity metadata is platform-specific; owner14-case execution is current macOS host evidence, not claimed Linux hosted qualification.
Only the explicitly assigned three publisher comparisons and one negative regression were changed by this reviewer; helper/harness/other source files remain unchanged.
The 14 process regressions ran on macOS with synthetic owned subprocesses; Linux execution remains for hosted CI.
Launch9 uses the actual local Chrome, PostgreSQL and Keycloak with read-only source mounts. No baked-image or hosted qualification is inferred.
Shared core and unrelated local projects were preserved. All full capability/profile/release obligations remain open.
